claims.text: Fare model decides the remedy, and this trip is an upfront-quoted one: EV-FARE-00517 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 28.00, both non-null, so POL-RD-02's metered recomputation does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however the trip is characterised. The live remedy is POL-RD-11(a): every dollar by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 is refunded in full.

The overcharge is arithmetic and it is the rider's own figure. charged_total is SGD 67.50 against a quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 28.00. The only properly chargeable pass-through on the ledger is the airport surcharge of SGD 6.00 - properly chargeable because the trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 3 (EV-TRIP-00517 pickup label), so POL-RD-09(4) does not touch that line; erp_gantries is empty and waiting_time_fee is 0.00, so nothing else is added back and there is no off-route ERP to double count under POL-RD-09(1). The excess is 67.50 - 28.00 - 6.00 = SGD 33.50, refundable in full under POL-RD-11(a). That is exactly the 'other 33' the rider says nobody can explain.

DISCLOSURE: EV-GPS-00517 is IMPAIRED - weight_multiplier 0.39, issue codes GPS_GAP (one gap of 620 s) and LOW_COVERAGE (coverage_pct 65.6) - and I cite it only for the negative finding that follows. On the trace the rider relies on, trace_distance_km is 19.9 km against an optimal of 19.6 km: an excess of 0.3 km and about 1.53%, so both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal) fail and no route deviation is established on this trip. Nothing in the distance or time lines of the fare_breakdown can therefore be justified by a deviation, and the SGD 39.50 charged over the quote stands unexplained on the platform's own evidence.

The impaired trace cannot be turned against the rider, and it does not force an escalation. POL-RD-07 bites only where a deviation is to be established on the gps_trace, and none is established here; POL-RD-07(ii) and POL-RD-10(3) are therefore not in play. The fact that decides this ruling - that charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd by SGD 33.50 with no chargeable basis - is carried by EV-FARE-00517 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) and EV-TRIP-00517 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0), so under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence is not capped by the 0.39 weight of a trace the money does not rest on.

Nothing in the record attributes the extra charge to the rider. The chat log for this trip is empty - message_count 0, messages [] - so there is no rider instruction identifying a place or road of the kind POL-RD-04 requires, and no waypoint_hint exists to corroborate one. The driver's own account, that his app crashed and later 'completed the trip by itself' and that he 'didn't choose the amount', describes a platform data failure rather than an entitlement to bill the rider for it; under POL-RD-11 the driver's unrecovered cost on an unjustified detour is not recoverable from the rider.

No external event exonerates any part of this fare. EV-ADVIS-00517-01 is MISSING - weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, 'no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window' - and its absence is itself citable. With no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, POL-RD-03 cannot be invoked to justify the route or the charge, and its absence cannot be cured by assertion under POL-RD-08.

The billed lines do not even reconcile with the rate card the ledger prints on its own face. time_charged_min is 30.0 at per_min_rate_sgd 0.28, which is SGD 8.40, not the SGD 40.50 time_fare actually billed; distance_charged_km is 19.9 at per_km_rate_sgd 0.75, which is SGD 14.925, not the SGD 16.40 distance_fare billed; surge_multiplier is 1.0 so no surge explains the gap. Both lines have counterparts on the trip record (30.0 minutes, 19.9 km), so this is a rate overcharge on the distance and time lines, not an unmatched charge line - and on an upfront-quoted fare those lines were fixed at booking in any event.

The rider is not a serial claimant and no extra corroboration burden attaches to her account. On EV-RPROF-00517 she has deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the POL-RD-08 hurdle that requires corroboration beyond the gps_trace where a rider has four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated does not apply, and nothing on her profile may be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

Honest concession, so that the arithmetic above is not inflated: the rider does not press a POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern. That clause runs on a MATERIAL deviation and none exists on this trip, and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 110, so both the three-flag test and the 5% test fail. The rider's case rests on this trip's ledger, not on the driver's history, which is what POL-GEN-01 requires.

claims.text: The route-deviation claim fails on this trip's own arithmetic, and POL-RD-01 fixes the consequence. A deviation is ESTABLISHED only where the excess exceeds 20% of the optimal distance AND exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms; the derived deviation block for EV-GPS-00517 records an excess of 0.3 km (1.53%) over a 19.6 km optimal, so both gates fail, no deviation exists, and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, save only for a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity refund. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 is admissibility-IMPAIRED at weight 0.39, issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

The distance field the tribunal must use is the trace's, not the ledger's convenience copy. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km governing where it and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, and on this record the trace distance is 19.9 km against a 19.6 km optimal route — 0.3 km of excess, an order of magnitude below the 0.8 km absolute gate. Disclosure: the trace artifact EV-GPS-00517 is impaired at weight 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

The rider carries the initial burden and cannot discharge it. POL-RD-08 requires the rider to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace or, where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), from an independent source named in the POL-RD-07(ii) list. This trace is impaired — the 620-second gap exceeds limb (a)'s 90 seconds — and no POL-RD-07(ii) source exists: EV-CHAT-00517 carries zero messages, EV-FARE-00517 charges no ERP gantry, the driver's account names no route, and trip_record.actual_distance_km (19.9 km) reproduces the trace figure rather than being independently derived from it. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 weighs 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

Even the impaired stretch is measured in the driver's favour. POL-RD-07(i) requires excess across a gap to be taken as the straight line between the bounding fixes, and the derived figures already do exactly that: the published 19.9 km trace distance includes the 6.89 km straight line across the 22:26:30 to 22:36:50 gap, which is why no excess beyond 0.3 km appears. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 is impaired at weight 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

There is no distance-or-time money in this dispute. The fare_breakdown's fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted fare of SGD 28.00, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the trip is characterised. Any residual question about the charged total is confined by POL-RD-11 to the pass-through and statutory lines and to a POL-RD-09 correction.

There is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity defect to carve out of that default. EV-FARE-00517 carries an empty erp_gantries list and tolls_erp of 0.00, so nothing was charged for a gantry the trace never crossed, and the SGD 6.00 airport surcharge is properly chargeable because this trip ORIGINATED at Changi Airport Terminal 3 (pickup label on EV-TRIP-00517) — it is not an airport surcharge on a trip that merely ends at an airport. POL-RD-09 therefore yields no correction against this fare.

No repeat-deviation pattern may be set against this driver. POL-RD-06 is the only route to an uplift or a conduct referral, and its test fails twice over: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, a ratio of 0.00 against the 0.05 threshold, and no MATERIAL deviation exists on this trace in any event. POL-GEN-01 is respected because no other profile field is relied on. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 is impaired at weight 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

Nothing external needs to be excused, and nothing external exists. EV-ADVIS-00517-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 (MISSING_ARTIFACT): no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window, so no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is in play — and equally no closure can be invoked to manufacture an excess. The absence is itself citable and leaves the trip on its ordinary route.

The driver's account of an app crash is corroborated by the shape of the artifact itself, not merely asserted. The driver track runs 22:11:40 to 22:41:40 with a single interruption of 620 seconds (22:26:30 to 22:36:50) — the signature of device telemetry dropping out and resuming at completion — while EV-CHAT-00517 records no message from either party and EV-FARE-00517 charges no gantry, so nothing in the record contradicts him and he is not shown to have chosen the fare. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 is impaired at weight 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

The present state should stand, or the matter should go to a human — not to a refund. On the deviation claim NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they are, which is the outcome the evidence supports; and if the judge considers the 620-second impairment leaves the route question genuinely unsettled, POL-RD-10(3) makes escalation mandatory on an impaired trace with no POL-RD-07(ii) corroboration, which holds the amount rather than issuing a monetary ruling. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 weighs 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is settled on the ledger, and the route argument does not change it.

HOW THE FARE IS HANDLED. EV-FARE-00517 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 28.00, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time lines were fixed at booking and the rider loses nothing on them however the trip was driven. The driver is right about that much. The ledger's own lines do not fit its printed rate card (30.0 min x 0.28 = 8.40, not the 40.50 time_fare; 19.9 km x 0.75 = 14.925, not the 16.40 distance_fare), and the rider is right to flag it, but on an upfront fare those lines are not the rider's risk and the discrepancy changes nothing in the refund arithmetic below.

THE ROUTE. EV-TRIP-00517 and EV-GPS-00517 describe the same trip. trace_distance_km 19.9 against optimal_distance_km 19.6 is an excess of 0.3 km, 1.53% - below both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km and 20% of optimal). No deviation is ESTABLISHED, on either side's reading, so no POL-RD-01/POL-RD-02 remedy arises and no POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04 or POL-RD-05 exoneration is needed (the chat log is empty and the advisory EV-ADVIS-00517-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0). The GPS trace is IMPAIRED: weight_multiplier 0.39, issue codes GPS_GAP (one 620 s gap, 22:26:30-22:36:50) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6%). Under POL-RD-07(i) that stretch is measured as the straight line between its bounding fixes, and the published 19.9 km already includes it. The impairment is named and disclosed, and it does not decide this case, because the money below does not rest on the trace.

THE REFUND (POL-RD-11(a)). The rider is refunded the amount by which charged_total (67.50) exceeds quoted_fare (28.00) plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The trip originates at Changi Terminal 3, so the airport surcharge IS properly chargeable; but the trip ran on Saturday 5 September 2026, pickup 22:05 SGT, which falls inside the policy's peak window (Friday/Saturday/Sunday 17:00-23:59), so the properly chargeable surcharge is the peak rate 8.00, not the 6.00 itemised on the ledger. ERP and tolls are 0.00 (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00) and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. Refund = 67.50 - 28.00 - 8.00 = 31.50. That is the unexplained "other 33" the rider asks about, adjusted for the surcharge rate: the rider's 33.50 claim is accepted in structure and corrected to 31.50.

NO_ACTION AND ESCALATION. The driver's fallback of NO_ACTION or escalation under POL-RD-10(3) is rejected. POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) exist so that a deviation is not "established" on an impaired trace without corroboration; here no deviation is established at all, the rider's money is carried by the ledger (EV-FARE-00517) and the trip record (EV-TRIP-00517), both weight 1.0, and the driver's own account - app crashed, trip "completed by itself", "I didn't choose the amount" - describes a platform fault, not an entitlement to bill for it. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, and NO_ACTION would simply leave an explained-nowhere 39.50 with the rider. No POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding arises (no phantom gantry, and the surcharge is validly applied to an airport-originating trip). No POL-RD-06 pattern exists (deviation_flags_90d 0 of 250 completed trips; no MATERIAL deviation), so there is no driver-conduct referral and no driver compensation (billed 19.9 km = trace 19.9 km, no unbilled kilometres). The profile counters relied on (deviation_flags_90d, completed_trips_90d, deviation_claims_60d) are the citable ones; POL-GEN-01 is respected on both sides. Referrals: none.

Confidence 0.85, below the 1.0 cap set by the weight of the artifacts carrying the deciding fact (EV-FARE-00517 and EV-TRIP-00517, each 1.0), and above the 0.70 floor, so no escalation. PARTIAL_REFUND: 31.50 to the rider.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — here is what I decided, and why.

The money. This trip was sold as an upfront-quoted fare: EV-FARE-00517 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 28.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02's metered recomputation does not run and no refund arises out of the route as such. The fare ledger shows charged_total 67.50 (EV-FARE-00517). On top of the 28.00 quote, the only properly chargeable extra is the 6.00 Changi Airport surcharge — properly chargeable because the trip ORIGINATED at Changi Airport Terminal 3 (EV-TRIP-00517 pickup label 'Changi Airport Terminal 3, Departure Level Door 5'), not because it merely ended near an airport. There are no ERP or toll charges to add back (erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp 0.00) and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. So the rider should have paid 28.00 + 6.00 = 34.00, and the amount charged over that — 67.50 − 34.00 = 33.50 — is refunded in full under POL-RD-11(a). That is the 'other 33'.

The route. No route deviation is established. On the trace the excess is 0.3 km, about 1.53% of the 19.6 km optimal route (EV-GPS-00517 derived figures; EV-TRIP-00517 optimal), and POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 0.8 km absolute and 20% of optimal — neither gate passes, so there is no deviation and no distance or time charge to disturb. No rider-requested detour was recorded either (EV-CHAT-00517 carries zero messages and no waypoint_hint), and no traffic advisory exists to exonerate or explain anything (EV-ADVIS-00517-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT).

The impaired trace, and why it does not escalate the case. EV-GPS-00517 is admissibility-IMPAIRED at weight 0.39 on issue codes GPS_GAP (one 620-second gap) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6% coverage), and I name it here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires. It is used only for the negative 'no deviation' finding, and it is read in the way most favourable to the driver (POL-RD-07(i): the gap is bridged by the 6.89 km straight line between the bounding fixes). It does not carry the money finding: the deciding figures — charged_total 67.50, quoted_fare 28.00, the empty gantry set and the 6.00 surcharge line — come from EV-FARE-00517, and the airport-origin fact from EV-TRIP-00517, both COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so confidence is not capped by the 0.39 (POL-GEN-02(2)). POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. That trigger, and POL-RD-07(ii)–(iii), exist for the case where a deviation has to be established on an impaired trace and no independent source of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names can carry it. Here nothing has to be established on the trace at all: the deviation fails on its own arithmetic in the driver's favour, and the refund is payable from the ledger alone, a matter the trace does not touch.

The driver's account. I accept the driver's explanation that his app crashed, that he dropped the rider at the hotel, and that the app later completed the trip by itself and he did not choose the amount. That is an honest account of a platform data failure, and nothing in the record contradicts it. It is not, however, a basis for keeping 33.50 that was never quoted and has no chargeable footing.

The driver's request for NO_ACTION, or alternatively for escalation. On the deviation the driver's advocate is right, and I have so found: there is no deviation, and no distance-or-time refund is added on that account. But NO_ACTION is not the consequence, because the rider's refund does not rest on a deviation. It rests on POL-RD-11(a), which returns the excess over the quote plus the properly chargeable pass-throughs whether or not a deviation exists. For the same reason POL-RD-10(3) does not make escalation mandatory — escalation on an impaired trace is what the policy gives where a deviation cannot be proved and the rider would otherwise lose on a data failure; here the rider is not losing on any data failure, so the amount is not held.

The rate card. One observation for the platform, which belongs here rather than in a referral: the ledger's own lines do not reconcile with the rate card it prints. 30.0 minutes at per_min_rate_sgd 0.28 is 8.40, not the 40.50 time_fare billed; 19.9 km at per_km_rate_sgd 0.75 is 14.925, not the 16.40 distance_fare billed; surge_multiplier is 1.0 and explains neither gap. On an upfront-quoted fare those lines do not drive the refund, so the amount above is unaffected, but the platform may wish to check how this rate card was applied to this trip.

Referrals. None are made, because no clause produces one. There is no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral: that clause needs a material deviation and a repeat pattern, and this trip has neither a material deviation nor a pattern (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250; the rider does not press it and it would fail if pressed). There is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral: no gantry was charged, and the airport surcharge is properly chargeable on a trip originating at the airport.

Outcome. PARTIAL_REFUND of 33.50 against the 67.50 charged. The charge stands as to the remaining 34.00 (the 28.00 quote plus the 6.00 airport surcharge). No driver compensation is due — the distance billed (19.9 km) is not less than the distance recorded, so no POL-RD-04 compensation arises. Confidence 0.90, above the 0.70 floor.

A deviation is ESTABLISHED only where the excess exceeds 20% of the optimal distance AND exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms; the derived deviation block for EV-GPS-00517 records an excess of 0.3 km (1.53%) over a 19.6 km optimal, so both gates fail, no deviation exists, and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, save only for a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity refund. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 is admissibility-IMPAIRED at weight 0.39, issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

The distance field the tribunal must use is the trace's, not the ledger's convenience copy. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km governing where it and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, and on this record the trace distance is 19.9 km against a 19.6 km optimal route — 0.3 km of excess, an order of magnitude below the 0.8 km absolute gate. Disclosure: the trace artifact EV-GPS-00517 is impaired at weight 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

The rider carries the initial burden and cannot discharge it. POL-RD-08 requires the rider to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace or, where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), from an independent source named in the POL-RD-07(ii) list. This trace is impaired — the 620-second gap exceeds limb (a)'s 90 seconds — and no POL-RD-07(ii) source exists: EV-CHAT-00517 carries zero messages, EV-FARE-00517 charges no ERP gantry, the driver's account names no route, and trip_record.actual_distance_km (19.9 km) reproduces the trace figure rather than being independently derived from it. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 weighs 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

Even the impaired stretch is measured in the driver's favour. POL-RD-07(i) requires excess across a gap to be taken as the straight line between the bounding fixes, and the derived figures already do exactly that: the published 19.9 km trace distance includes the 6.89 km straight line across the 22:26:30 to 22:36:50 gap, which is why no excess beyond 0.3 km appears. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 is impaired at weight 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

There is no distance-or-time money in this dispute. The fare_breakdown's fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted fare of SGD 28.00, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the trip is characterised. Any residual question about the charged total is confined by POL-RD-11 to the pass-through and statutory lines and to a POL-RD-09 correction.

There is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity defect to carve out of that default. EV-FARE-00517 carries an empty erp_gantries list and tolls_erp of 0.00, so nothing was charged for a gantry the trace never crossed, and the SGD 6.00 airport surcharge is properly chargeable because this trip ORIGINATED at Changi Airport Terminal 3 (pickup label on EV-TRIP-00517) — it is not an airport surcharge on a trip that merely ends at an airport. POL-RD-09 therefore yields no correction against this fare.

No repeat-deviation pattern may be set against this driver. POL-RD-06 is the only route to an uplift or a conduct referral, and its test fails twice over: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, a ratio of 0.00 against the 0.05 threshold, and no MATERIAL deviation exists on this trace in any event. POL-GEN-01 is respected because no other profile field is relied on. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 is impaired at weight 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

Nothing external needs to be excused, and nothing external exists. EV-ADVIS-00517-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 (MISSING_ARTIFACT): no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window, so no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is in play — and equally no closure can be invoked to manufacture an excess. The absence is itself citable and leaves the trip on its ordinary route.

The driver's account of an app crash is corroborated by the shape of the artifact itself, not merely asserted. The driver track runs 22:11:40 to 22:41:40 with a single interruption of 620 seconds (22:26:30 to 22:36:50) — the signature of device telemetry dropping out and resuming at completion — while EV-CHAT-00517 records no message from either party and EV-FARE-00517 charges no gantry, so nothing in the record contradicts him and he is not shown to have chosen the fare. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 is impaired at weight 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

The present state should stand, or the matter should go to a human — not to a refund. On the deviation claim NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they are, which is the outcome the evidence supports; and if the judge considers the 620-second impairment leaves the route question genuinely unsettled, POL-RD-10(3) makes escalation mandatory on an impaired trace with no POL-RD-07(ii) corroboration, which holds the amount rather than issuing a monetary ruling. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 weighs 0.39 on GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.
